cases.sentence: Все принимали участие в ___, кроме Кити и Левина.
cases.explain: «общем разговоре» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Everyone took part in the conversation except Kitty and Levin. At first, when they were talking of the influence that one people has on another, there rose to Levin’s mind what he had to say on the subject. But these ideas, once of such importance in his eyes, seemed to come into his brain as in a dream, and had now not the slightest interest for him. It even struck him as strange that they should be so eager to talk of what was of no use to anyone. Kitty, too, should, one would have supposed, have been interested in what they were saying of the rights and education of women. How often she had mused on the subject, thinking of her friend abroad, Varenka, of her painful state of dependence, how often she had wondered about herself what would become of her if she did not marry, and how often she had argued with her sister about it! But it did not interest her at all. She and Levin had a conversation of their own, yet not a conversation, but some sort of mysterious communication, which brought them every moment nearer, and stirred in both a sense of glad terror before the unknown into which they were entering.

cases.sentence: Сначала Левин, на вопрос Кити о том, как он мог видеть ее ___ в карете, рассказал ей, как он шел с покоса по большой дороге и встретил ее.
cases.explain: «прошлого года» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: At first Levin, in answer to Kitty’s question how he could have seen her last year in the carriage, told her how he had been coming home from the mowing along the high road and had met her.

cases.sentence: – Как хорошо смеется Туровцын! – сказал Левин, любуясь на его ___ и трясущееся тело.
cases.explain: «влажные глаза» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “How nicely Turovtsin laughs!” said Levin, admiring his moist eyes and shaking chest.

cases.sentence: – И я вижу, что вы думаете, что он ___?
cases.explain: «дурной человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “And I see you think he’s a horrid man?”

cases.sentence: И поскорей не думайте больше так! – сказала Кити. – Я тоже была о нем очень ___, но это, это – премилый и удивительно добрый человек.
cases.explain: «низкого мнения» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Oh, you’re wrong! And you must give up thinking so directly!” said Kitty. “I used to have a very poor opinion of him too, but he, he’s an awfully nice and wonderfully good-hearted man. He has a heart of gold.”

cases.explain: «большие друзья» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “We are great friends. I know him very well. Last winter, soon after … you came to see us,” she said, with a guilty and at the same time confiding smile, “all Dolly’s children had scarlet fever, and he happened to come and see her. And only fancy,” she said in a whisper, “he felt so sorry for her that he stayed and began to help her look after the children. Yes, and for three weeks he stopped with them, and looked after the children like a nurse.”
